name: runfile
description: Contributes VS Code tasks generated at runtime by a shell command, so a project's tasks appear in Run Task without ever being written to tasks.json.

task.description: The label of the generated task to run.

file.description: Path to the Runfile the target is resolved against (passed as `run -f`). Omit to let `run` discover the Runfile from the workspace folder.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No Runfile targets were found in this workspace.
[Refresh](command:runfile.refresh)

If you expected targets here, check the [output log](command:runfile.showLog) for a failing generate command.

runfile.generateCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command run in each workspace folder to produce the **task descriptors** JSON on **stdout** — the `{ "formatVersion": 1, "sources": [...] }` document emitted by `run :generate task-descriptors`. It always includes namespaced (`includes`) and machine-wide global targets. Anything written to stderr is ignored. The command is re-run every time VS Code fetches tasks — keep it cheap.

runfile.enabled.description: Contribute dynamically generated tasks. Turn off to stop running the generate command entirely.

runfile.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show an inline **Run** button above every target in a Runfile — any `Runfile*.json` or `Runfile*.json5`, at any depth, so files reached through `includes` (`Runfile-ci.json`, `Runfile.dev.json5`, …) are covered too. Each button runs that target from the file that defines it (`run --stdin-args -f <that file> <target>`), so a target inside an included Runfile runs under the name the file spells it with. Internal (`_`-prefixed) targets and targets carrying `metadata.excludeFromGenerateCommand` get no button.

runfile.interactive.markdownDescription: Run tasks that pass `--stdin-args` inside an interactive pseudoterminal so `run` can prompt for missing arguments and read your answers from the terminal. Turn off to run them as plain shell tasks (stdin prompts will fail, matching VS Code's default task behaviour).
